## Part 1: Nested-Fixable Estimation (ANIPW)

### The identification hierarchy

```
a-fixable  ⊂  p-fixable  ⊂  nested-fixable  ⊂  identified
```

A treatment is **nested-fixable** when the effect is identified by the
One-Line ID algorithm, but is **neither a-fixable nor p-fixable**. This
occurs when a *child* of the treatment shares a hidden common cause with
the treatment — so neither backdoor nor front-door adjustment is sufficient.

### Example: HIV treatment graph

This example comes from the anankeR estimation-strategies vignette.
A drug treatment T affects CD4 count (outcome), mediated partly through
Toxicity and Adherence. Hidden common causes link several variables.

```{julia}
g_hiv = make_graph(
    vertices = [:ViralLoad, :Income, :Exercise, :T, :Toxicity, :Adherence, :CD4],
    di_edges  = [
        (:ViralLoad, :T),       (:ViralLoad, :CD4),
        (:Income,    :T),       (:Exercise,  :CD4),
        (:T,         :Toxicity),(:T,          :CD4),
        (:Toxicity,  :Adherence),(:Adherence, :CD4),
    ],
    bi_edges  = [
        (:Income,    :Toxicity),
        (:Exercise,  :Income),
        (:Exercise,  :T),
        (:ViralLoad, :Adherence),
        (:ViralLoad, :CD4),
    ],
)
```

Toxicity is a **child** of T and also in T's **district** (through the
chain Exercise ↔ Income ↔ Toxicity), making T not p-fixable:

```{julia}
println("district(T)  = ", district(g_hiv, :T))
println("children(T)  = ", children(g_hiv, :T))
println()
println("is_fix(:T)   = ", is_fix(g_hiv, :T))
println("is_p_fix(:T) = ", is_p_fix(g_hiv, :T))

id_hiv = identify(g_hiv, :T, :CD4)
println("strategy     = ", id_hiv.strategy)
```

### Simulate data from the DGP

```{julia}
function sim_hiv(n; seed=42)
    Random.seed!(seed)
    # Latent hidden common causes
    U_EI   = randn(n)   # Exercise ↔ Income
    U_ET   = randn(n)   # Exercise ↔ T
    U_ITox = randn(n)   # Income ↔ Toxicity
    U_VA   = randn(n)   # ViralLoad ↔ Adherence
    U_VCD4 = randn(n)   # ViralLoad ↔ CD4

    ViralLoad = randn(n)
    Exercise  = randn(n) .+ 0.5 .* U_EI .+ 0.5 .* U_ET
    Income    = randn(n) .+ 0.4 .* ViralLoad .+ 0.4 .* U_EI .+ 0.4 .* U_ITox
    T         = Float64.(rand(n) .< logistic.(0.5 .* ViralLoad .+ 0.3 .* Income .+ 0.4 .* U_ET))
    Toxicity  = randn(n) .+ 0.6 .* T .+ 0.3 .* U_ITox
    Adherence = randn(n) .+ 0.5 .* Toxicity .+ 0.3 .* U_VA
    CD4       = randn(n) .+ 0.4 .* T .+ 0.3 .* Adherence .+
                            0.2 .* Exercise .+ 0.3 .* ViralLoad .+
                            0.3 .* U_VCD4 .+ 0.2 .* U_VA

    # True ACE(T=1 vs T=0):
    # Direct: 0.4
    # Indirect T→Tox→Adh→CD4: 0.6 × 0.5 × 0.3 = 0.09
    # Total ≈ 0.49

    DataFrame(ViralLoad=ViralLoad, Income=Income, Exercise=Exercise,
              T=T, Toxicity=Toxicity, Adherence=Adherence, CD4=CD4)
end

df_hiv = sim_hiv(2_000)
println("True ACE ≈ 0.49  (0.4 direct + 0.09 through Adherence)")
first(df_hiv, 3)
```

### Estimation

`estimate_causal()` detects nested-fixable and routes to ANIPW.

```{julia}
res_hiv = estimate_causal(
    a         = [1, 0],
    data      = df_hiv,
    graph     = g_hiv,
    treatment = :T,
    outcome   = :CD4,
)

println("True ACE ≈ 0.49")
@printf("ANIPW: ACE = %.3f  95%% CI (%.3f, %.3f)\n",
        res_hiv[:ANIPW].ACE, res_hiv[:ANIPW].lower_ci, res_hiv[:ANIPW].upper_ci)
@printf("NIPW:  ACE = %.3f\n", res_hiv[:NIPW].ACE)
```

### Nested rebalancing weights

The ANIPW estimator builds **nested rebalancing weights** through the
intrinsic kernel of each modified district. After reweighting, propensity
and outcome regression are estimated by weighted GLM.

```{julia}
rw = res_hiv[:rw]
@printf("Rebalancing weights — min: %.3f  max: %.3f  mean: %.3f\n",
        minimum(rw), maximum(rw), mean(rw))
```

## Part 2: Missing Data with FlexMissing.jl

When covariates are **missing at random** (MAR), `FlexMissing.jl` identifies
and estimates the missing-data propensity scores, producing per-row IPW
weights for `estimate_causal()`.

### Workflow

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using FlexMissing

# 1. Define the missingness DAG (mDAG)
mdag = FlexMissing.make_graph(
    obs_variables      = ["T", "CD4"],
    missing_variables  = ["ViralLoad"],
    missing_indicators = ["R_VL"],
    di_edges = [("ViralLoad","T"), ("ViralLoad","CD4"), ("ViralLoad","R_VL"),
                ("T","CD4")],
)

# 2. Identify and estimate missing-data propensities
ID    = FlexMissing.ID_algorithm(mdag)
props = FlexMissing.propensity(mdag, data_with_missing, ID; law=:target)

# 3. Build IPW weights on complete cases
obs = .!ismissing.(data_with_missing.ViralLoad)
wts = 1.0 ./ coalesce.(props["R_VL"].pred[obs], 1.0)

# 4. Estimate causal effect using IPW-weighted complete cases
result = estimate_causal(
    a=[1,0], data=dropmissing(data_with_missing),
    graph=g_hiv, treatment=:T, outcome=:CD4,
    sample_weights=wts,
)
```

### G2 graph (FlexMissing.jl)

The G2 example from `FlexMissing.jl` has six variables with complex
dependent missingness patterns. The full runnable code is in
`FlexMissing.jl/examples/01_identification.jl`.

```{julia}
#| eval: false
using FlexMissing

G2 = FlexMissing.make_graph(
    obs_variables=[], missing_variables=["X1","X2","X3","X4","X5","X6"],
    missing_indicators=["R1","R2","R3","R4","R5","R6"],
    di_edges=[
        ("X1","X2"),("X2","X3"),("X3","X4"),("X4","X5"),("X5","X6"),
        ("R6","R5"),("R6","R3"),("R5","R3"),("R4","R3"),("R3","R2"),("R2","R1"),
        ("X1","R3"),("X3","R4"),("X3","R5"),("X3","R6"),
        ("X4","R1"),("X4","R6"),("X5","R2"),("X6","R5"),
    ],
)
id = FlexMissing.ID_algorithm(G2; fulllaw=true)
FlexMissing.summarize_ID(id).target
```

## Summary

| Strategy | Condition | Estimator | Returns |
|---|---|---|---|
| a-fixable | `desc(A)∩dist(A) = {A}` | Backdoor TMLE | `:TMLE`, `:Onestep`, `:Gcomp`, `:IPW` |
| p-fixable | `dist(A)∩ch(A) = {}` | NPS-TMLE | `:TMLE`, `:Onestep` |
| nested-fixable | One-Line ID passes | ANIPW | `:ANIPW`, `:NIPW`, `:rw` |

All three strategies are accessible through `estimate_causal()` — routing
is automatic based on the graph structure.
